comments.comment: So I've just reached the point at 39:52, and I want to say as a (probably) cis woman who did think they were a trans man for a bit, that attempting a social transition when I wasn't actually trans was one of the most harrowing experiences I've ever had. My mental health was at its lowest point, if I'd tried to transition any longer I probably would have attempted suicide, and overall it was not a good solution to what I now recognise as intense internalised misogyny and anger at the way women are treated by society. The idea that a cis person could be tricked into transitioning by "the transes" is such a preposterous thing to me. The only thing "the transes" (and nonbinary people) influenced me to do was to take a critical look at my view of gender. I am now much more at peace thanks to that part of my life, because questioning the foundations of gender allowed me to recognise my own internalised misogyny, and to end a conflict with myself that had lasted from when I was 4 (and was first dismissed as a person for being a woman, never processed that anger properly), to when I was 18 and briefly thought I was trans.
